subject: general
question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

I feel frustrated that she __keeps reverting back to her bad habits__ after brief phases of positive change.

options.text: keeps reverting to her bad habits
keeps reverting backward to her bad habits
keeps reverting forth to her bad habits

solution:
The correct answer is '**keeps reverting to her bad habits**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The word "**revert**" inherently means "to go back" or "return to a previous state," so the use of "back" in the original sentence is redundant.
 
• Option 1, "**keeps reverting to her bad habits**," removes the redundancy and provides a grammatically correct and concise sentence.
 
• Option 2 ("**keeps reverting backward to her bad habits**") repeats the redundancy by adding "backward," which is unnecessary.
 
• Option 3 ("**keeps reverting forth to her bad habits**") is incorrect because "reverting forth" is not a valid usage of the verb "revert."
 
• Option 4 ("**No improvement required**") is incorrect because the original sentence contains redundancy that needs to be corrected.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"I feel frustrated that she **keeps reverting to her bad habits**__ after brief phases of positive change."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "keeps reverting backward to her bad habits" is incorrect because "reverting" already implies going back, making "backward" redundant.
 
• **Option 3:** "keeps reverting forth to her bad habits" is incorrect because "reverting forth" does not make sense in standard English usage.
 
• **Option 4:** "No improvement required" is incorrect because the original sentence has a redundancy that needs correction.
